caption_used: The performance of knowledge probing after editing with different editing methods on BioMedLM, where "Base" denotes LLM without editing. The x-axis shows co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale, while the y-axis represents accuracy (ACC %). All six methods show improving accuracy with increasing co-occurrence frequency. ROME consistently achieves the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 51% and reaching roughly 66% at the highest co-occurrence numbers. MEND and MEMIT follow as the next best performers, with MEND reaching approximately 56% and MEMIT approximately 55%. Notably, IKE demonstrates a steeper improvement rate than FT, surpassing it at co-occurrence numbers above 10^2 to reach approximately 52% at the highest frequency. The Base model exhibits the lowest performance throughout, plateauing at approximately 44%.
raw_response: DESCRIPTION: The figure is a multi-series line chart illustrating knowledge probing accuracy after applying different editing methods to BioMedLM as a function of co-occurrence frequency. The x-axis is labeled “Co-occurrence Number” and uses a logarithmic scale with major ticks at approximately 10, 100, and 1000, spanning from low single-digit values on the left to several thousand on the right. The y-axis is labeled “ACC (%)” on a linear scale, ranging roughly from 38% to 66% with tick marks at 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, and 65. Six colored lines with markers are shown: Base (black solid line with circle markers) increases from about 38% at the lowest co-occurrence to about 42% at the next point and then to about 44% by around 10^2, remaining near 44% through the highest co-occurrence. FT (blue solid line with downward triangle markers) rises from about 40% to ~43%, then ~46%, and ends near ~48%. IKE (red solid line with upward triangle markers) increases from about 43% to ~45%, then ~46.5%, and ends near ~49.5%. MEND (brown solid line with diamond markers) goes from about 44.5% to ~49%, then ~54%, and ends near ~56.5%. MEMIT (purple solid line with pentagon markers) starts near ~44%, rises to ~51%, then ~53%, and ends near ~55%. ROME (green solid line with square markers) is highest throughout, increasing from about 51% to ~57%, then ~62%, and ending near ~66%, with all series generally trending upward as co-occurrence number increases.
